newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P says affirms New South Wales ratings.
newsitem.headline: S&P says affirms New South Wales ratings.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp said on Wednesday it had affirmed the long term AAA and short-term A-1 plus local currency ratings of the state of New South Wales.
The ratings agency said the outlook was stable.
Also affirmed are the AAA/A1 plus local currency ratings on the New South Wales Treasury Corporation (TCorp).
The AA long term and A1 plus short term foreign currency ratings on the NSW state and TCorp are also affirmed.

The AA rating is constrained by the sovereign ceiling rating of AA for the Commonwealth of Australia, and the foreign currency rating outlook is positive, reflecting the outlook on the rating of the Commonwealth, S&P said.

The ratings reflect the modest level of the state's overall indebtedness, its satisfactory ongoing financial position and the government's commitment to a disciplined medium-term fiscal framework, as well as its diversified economic base.

"NSW has a mature and well diversified economy that contributes about 34 percent of Australia's gross domestic product, and an economy that exports about one-third of its output either overseas or interstate," said S&P.
"With agriculture and mining sectors being proportionately smaller than in other states, the NSW economy is less exposed to commodity cycles," it added.

On the outlook, S&P said the state's debt position is projected to remain at its current modest level on the basis of a continuation of the sound financial results of the state's trading enterprise sector, and the government delivering on its budgetary objectives in the 'General Government Debt Elimination Act'."
